lines.japanese:
「春希さぁ、月曜ゼミに来なかったよね？
あたしずっと待ってたのに」
lines.english: “Haruki, you didn’t come to seminar on Monday, did you? I waited and waited for you.”

lines.japanese:
「和泉は火曜ゼミに来なかったな。
俺ずっと待ってたのに」
lines.english: “And you weren’t at Tuesday’s seminar, Izumi. I waited and waited for you.”

lines.japanese:
「二日も待ちぼうけなんて、切ないじゃん？
先輩たちに春希の女やってるみたいに思われても、
そっちに迷惑がかかるだろうしさぁ」
lines.english: “Being stood up two days running is pretty heartbreaking, you know. And if the older students start thinking I’m your girlfriend, that could make things awkward for you.”

lines.japanese:
「そうだな、月曜にサボったのは俺が悪かった。
確かにそのことは謝る」
lines.english: “Fair enough. Skipping Monday was my fault. I do owe you an apology for that.”

lines.japanese:
「ま、お互いすれ違いを重ねても、
こうしてやっと水曜に巡り会えたんだから、
めでたしめでたし、と...」
lines.english: “Still, after missing each other again and again, we’ve finally been reunited on Wednesday. And they lived happily ever—”

lines.japanese:
「で、月曜のこと先輩たちに聞いて回ったけど、
お前、俺が来てないこと電話で確認しただけで、
実際には顔出さなかったんだってな」
lines.english: “Except I asked around about Monday. Apparently you only called to make sure I wasn’t there. You never showed your face either.”
“Ngh…”

lines.japanese:
「今週ゼミに来たのは
今日が初めてだというのが全員の統一見解だ。
何か申し開きは？」
lines.english: “The unanimous testimony is that today is your first appearance at seminar all week. How do you plead?”

lines.japanese: 「...電話かけただけでも乙女っぽくない？」
lines.english: “…Doesn’t calling you at least make me seem a little girlish?”

lines.japanese:
「お前、本当は水曜しか来ないつもりだろ？
そうなんだろ？」
lines.english: “You never intended to come any day but Wednesday, did you? Admit it.”

lines.japanese: 「春希、粘着だよ...」
lines.english: “Haruki, you’re so obsessive…”

lines.japanese: 水曜日。
lines.english: Wednesday.

lines.japanese:
俺と和泉の勉強会もとうとう三回目を迎え、
そろそろ夕飯のレパートリーが尽きつつある。
lines.english: Izumi and I have now reached our third study session, and I’m already running out of dinners I know how to make.

lines.japanese:
一回目がカレー、二回目がカレーだったから、
三回目は思い切って激辛カレーにしようかと悩む昨今だ。
lines.english: The first time had been curry. The second had been curry. So for the third, I was considering a bold departure: extra-hot curry.

lines.japanese:
...こいつなら大喜びでおかわりしそうなのが
ネタとしては面白味に欠けるけどな。
lines.english: The only hitch was that she’d probably love it and ask for seconds, which would ruin the joke.

lines.japanese:
「レポートはあと２回くらいで終わりそうだから、
進級はなんとかなりそうだけど...
和泉、お前四年になったらどうするつもりなんだよ？」
lines.english: “Another two sessions or so should finish the paper, so I think you’ll scrape through to next year. But Izumi, what are you going to do once you’re a senior?”

lines.japanese:
なんて、和泉に関しては数時間先の未来よりも、
一年後の未来の方がよっぽど心配だったりする。
lines.english: Where Izumi was concerned, her prospects a year from now worried me far more than anything that might happen in the next few hours.

lines.japanese:
「他の連中はもうとっくに
卒論のネタ探しとかやってるのに.........何だよ？」
lines.english: “Everyone else has been looking for thesis topics for ages… What?”

lines.japanese:
けど、そんな俺の真摯な心配をよそに、
和泉の方は、なにを考えてるかわからない
ぼけっとした表情で、俺の顔を見つめていた。
lines.english: But oblivious to my sincere concern, Izumi merely stared at my face, blank and unreadable.

lines.japanese:
「春希さぁ...
思ったよりも、ほんの少し元気だね？」
lines.english: “Haruki… you seem just a tiny bit better than I expected.”

lines.japanese:
「国文にいる奴が嘆かわしい言葉の使い方するな。
俺はいつもこんなもんだ」
lines.english: “That’s an appalling choice of words from a Japanese literature major. I’m the same as ever.”

lines.japanese: 「もうちょっとヘコんでるかと思ったんだけどねぇ」
lines.english: “I thought you’d be a little more crushed.”

lines.japanese: 「意味がわからん」
lines.english: “I have no idea what you’re talking about.”

lines.japanese:
そんな二日前...
いや、昨夜までの俺を持ち出されても、
こいつの言いたいことなんか理解できるはずもない。
lines.english: Even if she meant the me from two days ago—no, from as recently as last night—I had no way to know what she was getting at.

lines.japanese:
「結構しぶといねぇ。
もうちょっと弱み見せてくれてもいいのにさ」
lines.english: “You’re harder to break than I thought.You could at least show me a little weakness.”

lines.japanese:
「今度は何を言ったのかすらわからん。
人と話すときはちゃんと聞こえるように喋れ」
lines.english: “This time I couldn’t even hear what you said. If you’re talking to someone, speak up.”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese:
「それと、人と話すときはそうやって目をそらすな...
どうした？」
lines.english: “And if you’re talking to someone, don’t look away like that… What is it?”
“Back from the dead…”
“What?”

lines.japanese:
和泉が目をそらした方向に俺も目を向けると、
そこは見慣れた大学の正門で。
lines.english: I followed Izumi’s gaze and found myself looking at the university’s familiar main gate.
“Sugiura…”
“Hmm?”

lines.japanese:
正門のところに、人待ち顔の、
最近見慣れてしまった少女。
lines.english: Waiting by the gate stood a girl I had grown rather too accustomed to seeing lately.

lines.japanese:
舞台の上に立っているのは、
この間ここで遭遇したときと全く同じキャストたち。
lines.english: The stage was set with precisely the same cast as the last time we had met here.

lines.japanese:
けれど、この間ここで遭遇したときと、
少し違う展開が待っていた。
lines.english: This time, however, the scene was about to play out a little differently.

lines.japanese:
「来るよ？
どうする？　また追い払う？」
lines.english: “She’s coming over. What do we do? Want me to chase her off again?”

lines.japanese:
「いや、いいよ。
もう、色々とバレてるから」
lines.english: “No, it’s fine. She knows what’s going on now.”
“Hmm…?”

lines.japanese:
俺の姿を見つけた杉浦小春は、
隣に和泉がいるにも関わらず、
そちらには目もくれずに俺に近づく。
lines.english: The moment Koharu Sugiura spotted me, she headed straight toward me without so much as glancing at Izumi beside me.

lines.japanese:
...ついでに言えば、
ここが大学正門前だということにも
目もくれてなかった。
lines.english: For that matter, she paid no attention to where we were: right outside the university gates.

lines.japanese:
「こんにちは、北原先輩。
...土曜はお疲れさまでした」
lines.english: “Hello, Mr. Kitahara. And… thank you for everything on Saturday.”

lines.japanese:
「あの後大丈夫だったか？
ちゃんと駅からタクシー拾っただろうな？」
lines.english: “Were you all right afterward? Tell me you took a taxi from the station.”
“Hmm…?”

lines.japanese:
雪菜を見つけた後、杉浦はいつの間にか姿を消していた。
だから、実は終電に乗れたか確認できてなかった。
lines.english: Sugiura had disappeared at some point after we found Setsuna. I’d never actually learned whether she made the last train.

lines.japanese:
「ご心配なく。
きちんと無事に、何事もなく帰宅しました」
lines.english: “You needn’t worry. I arrived home safely and without incident.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか...ならいい」
lines.english: “Good. I’m glad to hear it.”

lines.japanese: 「...まぁ、タクシー代は凄いことになりましたけどね」
lines.english: “…Though the taxi fare was rather spectacular.”

lines.japanese:
けれど、こうして目の前に無事な姿を見せてくれたことで、
とりあえずあの日の心配事がまた一つ片づいた。
lines.english: Still, seeing her safe and sound in front of me put one more of that night’s worries to rest.

lines.japanese: 「ねぇ、ちょっと...」
lines.english: “Hey, hang on…”

lines.japanese:
「すいませんが先輩...
少し、二人きりで話したいことがあるんですが」
lines.english: “I’m sorry, but there’s something I’d like to discuss with you in private.”

lines.japanese: 「ぅぉ～ぃ」
lines.english: “Heeey!”

lines.japanese:
...のはいいんだけど、なんだか今日、
新たな心配事が生まれそうな気配もしないでも。
lines.english: That was all very well, but I had the uneasy feeling a brand-new worry was about to take its place.

lines.japanese:
「時間は取らせません。
ほんの５分でいいです」
lines.english: “I won’t keep you long. Five minutes is all I need.”
“Uh, sure…”

lines.japanese: 杉浦はあくまで俺の方を睨みつける。
lines.english: Sugiura kept her glare fixed firmly on me.

lines.japanese:
それは、俺に非友好的な態度を取っているというより、
和泉を意図的に避けてると言った方が正しい態度のようで。
lines.english: It felt less like hostility toward me than a deliberate refusal to acknowledge Izumi.

lines.japanese:
ま、わからなくもないけど。
...本気で信じてたからなぁ、こいつの戯れ言。
lines.english: I could hardly blame her. She’d believed every word of Izumi’s nonsense.

lines.japanese:
「その、和泉。
悪いけど...」
lines.english: “Izumi, I’m sorry, but…”

lines.japanese:
「あたし捨てて付属のコに走るんだね...
春希ってやっぱり色男で年下殺しで犯罪者で...」
lines.english: “So you’re throwing me over for a girl from Houjou High… Haruki, you really are a lady-killer, a cradle-robber, a criminal…”

lines.japanese:
「もう二度とレポートなんて見てやんねぇ。
とっとと帰れ。『後輩』」
lines.english: “I am never helping you with another paper. Go home, ‘underclassman.’”

lines.japanese:
「冗談、じょ～だんだって！
コンビニで時間潰してくるから迎えに来てね～。
それじゃ、ど～ぞごゆっくり～！」
lines.english: “Kidding! I’m ki-idding! I’ll kill time at the convenience store, so come get me when you’re done. Enjoy yourse-elves!”

lines.japanese:
「見たか？
あれが前、君が疑ってた『俺の彼女』の正体だ」
lines.english: “There. Now you’ve met the woman you thought was ‘my girlfriend.’”

lines.japanese:
「.........本当はすごく面白い人だったんですね。
あまり側にいて欲しいタイプじゃありませんが」
lines.english: “…She’s much funnier than I realized. I’m not sure I’d want her around very often.”

lines.japanese:
まぁ、俺よりガチガチな彼女にとっては、
あの嘘つきでいい加減なちゃらんぽらんとは
相性悪いだろうな。
lines.english: Sugiura was even more straitlaced than I was. Of course she and that lying, irresponsible disaster of a woman wouldn’t get along.

lines.japanese:
「で...喫茶店にでも行くか？
ここで立ち話ってのもなんだし」
lines.english: “So… want to find a café? We don’t have to stand here talking.”

lines.japanese:
「ここで結構です。
大した話でもないので。
...お友達を待たせても可哀想ですから」
lines.english: “Here is fine. It isn’t anything important. And… I’d hate to keep your friend waiting.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか、わかった」
lines.english: “All right, then.”

lines.japanese:
でも、ま、そんな和泉を気づかってくれてることも、
あいつのことをちゃんと『ただの友達』と
認識してくれたことも、俺にとっては大きな前進だ。
lines.english: Still, her consideration for Izumi—and her new understanding that Izumi was just a friend—amounted to enormous progress as far as I was concerned.

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese:
「...思ったより、ちょっとは元気みたいですね。
もっと落ち込んでるかと思ってました」
lines.english: “…You seem a little better than I expected too. I thought you’d be much more depressed.”
“Not this again…”
“What?”

lines.japanese:
表現が微妙なところまで一緒だ。
確かこのコも来年文学部のはずなのに...
lines.english: Even the oddly hedged wording was the same. And she was supposed to be entering the literature department next year too…

lines.japanese:
「ま、みんな無事だったし。
騒いだ割には全然拍子抜けで終わったし」
lines.english: “Everyone came out of it safe. For all the noise I made, the whole thing ended up being a complete anticlimax.”

lines.japanese:
「無事だったのは彼女一人だけです。
あとの人たちは、先輩の大騒動に巻き込まれて、
大変な目に遭ってましたよ？」
lines.english: “She was the only one who came out of it unscathed. Everyone else got dragged into the uproar you caused and had an awful time.”

lines.japanese:
「パーティ会場のお店の人は脅されるし、
幹事さんは全員に連絡取らされるし、
挙げ句の果てにお友達まで巻き込んで...」
lines.english: “You threatened the staff at the party venue, forced the organizer to call every guest, and even dragged your friends into it…”

lines.japanese:
「わざわざ付属から徒歩１分もかけて、
言いたいことはそれだけか？」
lines.english: “Did you really walk a whole minute from Houjou High just to tell me that?”

lines.japanese:
彼女の場合、いくらお互いの関係に進展が見られても、
その歯に衣着せぬ物言いが変わることはないんだな...
lines.english: No matter how close we became, Sugiura was never going to soften a single word.

lines.japanese: 「先輩を叱りに来ました」
lines.english: “I came to tell you off.”

lines.japanese: 「もう何度も叱られてる」
lines.english: “You’ve done that several times already.”

lines.japanese:
『ほら、この通り』
...と言いたくなるくらい、予想通りの言葉が出てくる。
lines.english: There it was, right on cue—as if she had set out to prove my point for me.

lines.japanese:
「今までみたいに細かいことじゃないです。
先輩の性根を叩き直しに来たんです」
lines.english: “Not over the usual little things. I came to straighten you out once and for all.”

lines.japanese: 「...ホント、怖いもの知らずだな、杉浦は」
lines.english: “…You really don’t know when to be afraid, do you, Sugiura?”

lines.japanese:
「自分でもそう思いますけど...
今度ばかりは黙っていられなかったんです」
lines.english: “I know. But this time I couldn’t keep quiet.”

lines.japanese:
「この数日間で、
君が黙ったことなんか見たことないけどな」
lines.english: “I haven’t seen you keep quiet once in the past few days.”

lines.japanese:
「ちょっと黙っててください。
話があるのはこっちですよ？」
lines.english: “Would you please be quiet? I’m the one who came here to talk.”

lines.japanese:
三年前の俺とだったら、
いつまで経っても話が進まなかっただろうな。
lines.english: If she’d been arguing with the person I was three years ago, we would never have got anywhere.

lines.japanese:
だから今となっては、
ほんの少し大人になった俺の方が退くことで
バランスを取るしかない。
lines.english: Now that I was a tiny bit more mature, the only way to balance us was for me to back down.

lines.japanese: 「...学園祭のビデオ見ました」
lines.english: “…I watched the video from the school festival.”
“Not that again…”

lines.japanese:
かずさがあんなことになって以来、
随分と流通してるみたいだな、あれ。
lines.english: Ever since everything happened with Kazusa, that recording seemed to have gone into remarkably wide circulation.

lines.japanese:
「それに、小木曽から先輩たちの話聞きました。
...主に付属時代のことしか知らないみたいでしたけど」
lines.english: “Takahiro told me about the three of you too. Though most of what he knew was from your days at Houjou High.”

lines.japanese: 「なんでそんなこと...」
lines.english: “Why would you—”

lines.japanese:
俺にとっては思い出したくない...
いや、思い出すことすら必要ない、
ちっとも奥にしまわれてない、鮮やかな記憶。
lines.english: For me it was a memory I didn’t want to revisit—no, a memory I never needed to revisit, because it had never been put away at all. It remained as vivid as ever.

lines.japanese:
「お節介だと思います？
...わたしもそう思います」
lines.english: “You think I’m interfering, don’t you? So do I.”

lines.japanese: 「自覚あるなら...」
lines.english: “If you know that, then—”

lines.japanese:
「先輩こそ自覚あるなら、
いつまであんな態度でいるつもりなんですか？」
lines.english: “And if you know what you’re doing, how long are you going to keep treating her like that?”

lines.japanese: 「な...なにが？」
lines.english: “W-what are you talking about?”

lines.japanese:
「学園祭ではあんなに楽しそうだったのに。
すごくいい雰囲気だったのに...」
lines.english: “You both looked so happy at the festival. You seemed so right together…”
“Urgh…”

lines.japanese: まずったなぁ...
lines.english: I’d really screwed up.

lines.japanese:
「どうして今の二人は、
あんなことになってるんですか？」
lines.english: “How did the two of you end up like this?”

lines.japanese:
よりによって、一番知られてはならない相手に、
一番クリティカルなところを見せてしまうなんて...
今までの人生の中でも、五本の指に入る不覚。
lines.english: Of all people, the one person I could never afford to look weak in front of had caught me at my most vulnerable. Easily one of the five worst blunders of my life.

lines.japanese:
「『関係ない』とか『興味ない』とか強がってるけど、
本当はものすごく気にかけてたじゃないですか。
彼女が危険だったら、なりふり構わないじゃないですか」
lines.english: “You keep pretending it has nothing to do with you, that you don’t care, but you were desperately worried about her. The moment you thought she might be in danger, you stopped caring how it looked.”

lines.japanese:
俺の弱みをこんなふうに利用されるくらいなら、
それこそ毎日の学食代のネタにされた方がまだましだ。
lines.english: If she was going to use my weakness against me like this, I’d rather she blackmail me for lunch money every day.

lines.japanese:
「そんなに未練たらたらでいながら、
彼女のこと諦めるなんて納得できません！
今別れてしまったら、絶対に駄目です！」
lines.english: “You’re plainly nowhere near over her, so I refuse to accept that you’re giving up. You absolutely cannot let the two of you end things now!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あのなぁ...いや、はぁ...」
lines.english: “Now listen… No, never mind. God…”

lines.japanese:
前々から、人の事情に踏み込みすぎる奴だとは
思っていたけれど...
lines.english: I had long known she was too ready to barge into other people’s affairs.

lines.japanese:
もう、ここまで堂々と土足で踏み込んで来られると、
怒りの言葉よりも、感嘆のため息の方が先に出てしまう。
lines.english: But she barged so brazenly into my private life that astonishment beat anger to the punch. All I could do was sigh.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、杉浦」
lines.english: “Listen, Sugiura.”

lines.japanese: 「なんですか？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese:
「言ってることはともかく、
今の君のスタンスは絶対に間違ってると思うぞ？」
lines.english: “Never mind whether you’re right. You’re completely out of line here.”

lines.japanese:
「先輩がいくら正論で逃げようとしても、
わたしの意見を変えるつもりはありませんから」
lines.english: “You can hide behind all the impeccable logic you like. I’m not changing my mind.”

lines.japanese:
「俺のこと、どっちかと言えば嫌いだろ？
なのになんで...」
lines.english: “You dislike me more than you like me, don’t you? So why—”

lines.japanese: 「先輩なんかのためじゃありません」
lines.english: “I’m not doing it for you.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ一体誰の...あ」
lines.english: “Then who are you doing it for…? Oh.”

lines.japanese: 忘れてた...
lines.english: I’d forgotten.

lines.japanese:
「だって泣いてたじゃないですか。
彼女、泣いてたじゃないですか！」
lines.english: “Because she was crying. She was crying!”

lines.japanese:
そういえばこのコは、
雪菜と、会ってしまったんだ。
lines.english: Of course. Sugiura had met Setsuna.

lines.japanese: 終電間際の改札で、ぽつんと一人。
lines.english: Alone by the ticket gates, just before the last train.

lines.japanese:
俯いて、帰る気配もなくて、
ただ、人の波に取り残されてた少女を、
目の当たりにしてしまったんだ。
lines.english: Head bowed, making no move to go home, simply left behind by the passing tide of people—Sugiura had seen that girl with her own eyes.

lines.japanese:
「わたし、そういうの我慢できないんです。
お互いが好きなら上手く行ってくれないと困るんです」
lines.english: “I can’t bear things like that. If two people love each other, I need them to make it work.”

lines.japanese: 「困るって...」
lines.english: “You need them to?”

lines.japanese:
「だって自分なら...
好きな相手に冷たい態度取られるのは我慢できません」
lines.english: “Because if it were me… I couldn’t bear it if someone I loved turned cold toward me.”

lines.japanese: ある意味、ものすごい利己主義なお節介。
lines.english: It was meddling born of the most astonishing kind of self-interest.

lines.japanese:
「しかも相手が、本当は自分のことを
まだ好きでいてくれるなんて知ってたら、
余計に辛すぎて、どうしたらいいかわかりません」
lines.english: “And if I knew they really did still love me, it would hurt even more. I wouldn’t know what to do.”

lines.japanese:
自分が信じる正しいあり方のために、
とうとう、自分の親友の関係者の、
そのまた関係者にまで介入を始めた。
lines.english: In the name of her own idea of right and wrong, she’d started meddling with someone connected to her best friend—and now with someone connected to them.

lines.japanese:
「だから先輩も諦めないで欲しいんです。
もし、彼女に直接会うのがまだ辛いんだったら、
わたしが間に入っても...」
lines.english: “That’s why I don’t want you to give up either. If seeing her yourself is still too painful, I could act as a go-between—”

lines.japanese:
「って、ちょっと待て。
まったくの無関係者だろ杉浦は...」
lines.english: “Wait. Stop right there. You have absolutely nothing to do with this, Sugiura.”

lines.japanese:
「友達のお姉さんです。
行方探しだってしました。
それに...バイト先の先輩の彼女です！」
lines.english: “She’s my friend’s older sister. I helped look for her. And she’s… my coworker’s girlfriend!”

lines.japanese: なんという屁理屈。
lines.english: What breathtaking sophistry.

lines.japanese:
おそらく他人が同じ事を言ったら、
もの凄い勢いで噛みつくんだろうな。
lines.english: If anyone else offered her the same argument, she would probably tear them apart for it.

lines.japanese: 「ついでに、わたしのためでもあります」
lines.english: “And while we’re at it, I am doing this partly for myself.”
“Why…?”

lines.japanese:
「もし先輩の心の重荷が取れたら...
今みたいにひねくれた先輩じゃなくて、
もう少しわたしに優しい先輩になってくれると思うから」
lines.english: “Because if that weight were lifted from you, I think you might stop being so bitter and be a little kinder to me.”
“Listen…”

lines.japanese: 本当に、なんて迂遠な...
lines.english: What an unbelievably roundabout way…

lines.japanese:
そして、なんて無駄だらけで、
意味もなく壮大な計画なんだろう。
lines.english: What a wasteful, needlessly grandiose plan.

lines.japanese: 「なんて奴だ、君は」
lines.english: “You are unbelievable.”

lines.japanese: 「...怒りますか？」
lines.english: “…Are you angry?”

lines.japanese:
「...って、もういい。
好きにしてくれ」
lines.english: “…Oh, forget it. Do whatever you like.”

lines.japanese: もはや、呆れてものも...
lines.english: I was quite literally beyond…
“…Phew.”

lines.japanese: 「...今度は何だよ？」
lines.english: “…What now?”

lines.japanese:
とうとう匙を投げた俺をじっと見つめると、
杉浦は逆八の字だった眉を、軽く八の時に戻す。
lines.english: She studied me as I finally surrendered, and the angry slant of her brows eased gently downward.

lines.japanese:
「やっぱり、少しだけ立ち直りかけてるみたいですね。
よかった、ちょっと心配してたのは本当なんですよ」
lines.english: “You really do seem to be starting to recover, just a little. I’m glad. I truly was worried about you.”

lines.japanese: 「立ち直りかけてる？　俺が？」
lines.english: “Starting to recover? Me?”

lines.japanese:
「だって今日は、
わたしと同じレベルで言い争いしないですから」
lines.english: “You haven’t once sunk to my level and argued with me today.”
“Oh…”

lines.japanese:
軽く唇を開いて、
悪戯っぽい微笑みを漏らす。
lines.english: Her lips parted, and a mischievous smile slipped out.

lines.japanese:
「杉浦...もしかしてそれを確かめるために、
わざと俺を挑発したのか？」
lines.english: “Sugiura… did you deliberately provoke me just to test that?”

lines.japanese:
「まさか。
全部本気で言ってますよ？」
lines.english: “Of course not. I meant every word.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうなんだ...」
lines.english: “Oh. Right…”

lines.japanese:
そんな態度の急変も、
どっかの策士とは違って、
自然にこぼれ出てきたものらしかった。
lines.english: Unlike a certain schemer I knew, her sudden change of mood appeared to have come entirely naturally.

lines.japanese: 「とりあえず、これで説教は終わりです」
lines.english: “In any case, that concludes the lecture.”

lines.japanese: 「説教、ね」
lines.english: “A lecture, huh.”

lines.japanese:
こんなことなら、
無理やりにでも喫茶店に連れ込むべきだった。
lines.english: If I’d known this was coming, I should have dragged her into a café whether she liked it or not.

lines.japanese:
俺たちの妙な言い争いは、
正門を行き来する数百人の大学生や付属生に、
思いっきり誤解と憶測と妄想を与えたことだろう。
lines.english: Our bizarre quarrel must have given the hundreds of university and high school students passing through the main gate plenty to misunderstand, speculate about, and fantasize over.

lines.japanese:
「さっき言ったことに、嘘はありません。
これからも先輩がウジウジしてたら、
わたし、本当に小木曽さんに会いに行きますよ？」
lines.english: “I meant what I said. If you keep wallowing like this, I really will go see Setsuna.”

lines.japanese:
「わかったわかった。
とりあえず、気持ちだけ受け取っとく」
lines.english: “All right, all right. I appreciate the thought, at least.”

lines.japanese: でも、今はそういうことがあまり気にならない。
lines.english: But for once, I didn’t care about any of that.

lines.japanese:
「そこまで豪語するんなら、
ちゃんと結果を見せてくださいよ？」
lines.english: “If you’re going to talk that big, you’d better show me some results.”

lines.japanese:
杉浦の、あまりにまっすぐで、
鬱陶しい気持ちに中てられたからかもしれない。
lines.english: Perhaps Sugiura’s painfully earnest and exasperating concern had rubbed off on me.
lines.japaneseRuby:
杉浦の、あまりにまっすぐで、
鬱陶しい気持ちに[R中^あ]てられたからかもしれない。

lines.japanese:
「それじゃ俺、行くから。
人、待たせてるし」
lines.english: “I should go. I have someone waiting.”

lines.japanese:
「はい、お疲れさまでした。
わたしも帰ります」
lines.english: “All right. Thank you for your time. I’m going home too.”

lines.japanese:
彼女に明確な答えは示せないけれど、
でも、明確な否定を示す気も起こらなかった。
lines.english: I couldn’t give her a definite answer, but neither did I feel like rejecting the possibility outright.

lines.japanese:
だからつまり...
そこにある可能性は、ゼロなわけじゃないはずで、
だとしたら、声も心も荒げる必要なんて...
lines.english: Which meant… there was still a chance. And if there was, there was no need to raise my voice or let it upset me…

lines.japanese: 「あ、先輩！」
lines.english: “Wait!”
“Yes?”

lines.japanese:
そんな『前のこと』をいつの間にか考えられていた俺に、
背中から、もう一度快活な声がかけられる。
lines.english: I had found myself able to think about what came next, and her bright voice called me back from behind.

lines.japanese:
「わたし、今週は土日ともバイト入れてます。
先輩がうるさいんで、とりあえず二日とも早番です」
lines.english: “I’m working both Saturday and Sunday this week. Since you made such a fuss, I’m on the early shift both days.”
“…And?”

lines.japanese:
「っ！
それだけです！
じゃあ！」
lines.english: “Hmph! That’s all! Goodbye!”
“Huh…?”

lines.japanese: 今のは...なんだろう？
lines.english: What had that been about?

lines.japanese:
来るなってことなのか？
それとも...？
lines.english: Was she telling me not to come? Or was she…?
“Heeey.”
“Hmm?”

lines.japanese: 「さっきのコ、いつの間に仲良くなったの？」
lines.english: “When did you get so friendly with that girl?”

lines.japanese:
「まぁ、ひょんなことからって言うか、
ちょっとした誤解がきっかけって言うか」
lines.english: “It just sort of happened. You might say it started with a small misunderstanding.”

lines.japanese: 「誤解？」
lines.english: “A misunderstanding?”

lines.japanese:
「誰かが自分のこと俺の彼女って吹聴したらしくてな。
それで色々あって」
lines.english: “Apparently someone went around claiming to be my girlfriend. One thing led to another.”

lines.japanese:
「...蒸し返すね。
やっぱ春希って粘着？
ベッドの上でもやたらしつこいとか？」
lines.english: “…Still dragging that up? Maybe you really are obsessive, Haruki. Are you the kind who never knows when to quit in bed?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ言えばこう言う...」
lines.english: “Whatever I say, you always have an answer…”

lines.japanese:
「む～。
春希のためを思って悪役に徹したのに。
こういうのを『梯子を外される』って言うんだよね～」
lines.english: “Hmph. I went to all that trouble playing the villain for you. This is what they call having the rug pulled out from under you.”

lines.japanese:
「誰も感謝してないとか余計なお世話だとか
空気読めよとか使えない奴だなとか
そんなこと一言も言ってないだろ？」
lines.english: “I never once said that nobody appreciated it, or that you were meddling, or that you should learn to read the room, or that you were completely useless, did I?”

lines.japanese: 「しかも恩を仇で返されてる～！？」
lines.english: “And now you’re repaying kindness with cruelty!”

lines.japanese:
「冗談だ。和泉には感謝してる。
...けど、ま、あの件だけは無駄だったな」
lines.english: “I’m joking. I am grateful, Izumi. Though I admit that particular performance was wasted.”

lines.japanese:
「春希のために慣れない女切り売りしたのに...
ここまで報われないとかえって女っぽいよね」
lines.english: “I parceled out my meager supply of womanhood for you, and it got me nothing. If anything, that makes me feel even more feminine.”

lines.japanese:
「あ～もう全面的に謝る。
謝るからこの話題やめてくれ」
lines.english: “All right, I apologize for everything. I’m sorry. Just drop it.”

lines.japanese:
和泉はいつものように、
俺の部屋で自分の部屋以上にくつろぎながら、
でも今日は、ちょっと恨み節が厳しめだった。
lines.english: As usual, Izumi had made herself even more at home in my apartment than in her own. Today, though, she was laying the guilt on a little thicker.

lines.japanese:
「ま、でもさ...
やっぱ、ちょっと変わったよね、春希」
lines.english: “Still… you really have changed a little, Haruki.”

lines.japanese:
「そっか？
どこがだよ？」
lines.english: “Have I? How?”

lines.japanese:
「あたし以外の女に対しても
拒否反応出なくなってるし」
lines.english: “You don’t recoil from every woman who isn’t me anymore.”
“That’s…”

lines.japanese:
「落ち込んでたところを誰かに励ましてもらった？
だから、女に対しての苦手意識が薄れてるのかな？」
lines.english: “Did someone cheer you up when you were down? Maybe that’s made you less uncomfortable around women.”

lines.japanese: 「.........別に、落ち込むことなんか何もなかった」
lines.english: “…There was never anything for me to be down about.”

lines.japanese:
俺の知ってる女の中で一番女っぽくないくせに、
なんか女の勘っぽいところだけは鋭いな、こいつ。
lines.english: For the least feminine woman I knew, she had a surprisingly sharp feminine intuition.

lines.japanese:
「あ～あ、つまらん。
子供に親離れされてくのって、こんな感じなのかな？」
lines.english: “How dull. Is this what it feels like when your child stops needing you?”

lines.japanese: 「だから何もなかったって...」
lines.english: “I told you, nothing happened…”

lines.japanese: けど...そうなのか？
lines.english: But… was she right?

lines.japanese: 端から見ると、少し変わってるように見えるのか、俺？
lines.english: Did I really seem different to other people?

lines.japanese:
あんなことがあったのに。
いや、逆にあんなことがあったからこそ...
lines.english: After what had happened. Or perhaps precisely because it had happened…

lines.japanese:
「ドラマは起こらず、かな...
ま、でも、それでもいっか」
lines.english: “So much for the drama… Still, maybe that’s all right.”

lines.japanese: 「なんか言ったか？」
lines.english: “Did you say something?”

lines.japanese:
「お～な～か～す～い～た～！
ごはんごはん～！」
lines.english: “I’m hu-ungry! Food, food, food!”

lines.japanese:
「お前はここに何しに来てるんだよ...
できるまで大人しくレポートやってろ！」
lines.english: “What do you think you come here for? Work on your paper and keep quiet until dinner’s ready!”

lines.japanese:
自分の気持ちを諦めない粘り強さが...
和泉の言う『粘着』が、身についてきたんだろうか？
lines.english: Was I learning the tenacity not to give up on my own feelings—the ‘obsession,’ as Izumi called it?

lines.japanese: 「春希～、あんたの電話～」
lines.english: “Haruki, your phone’s ringing.”

lines.japanese:
「ちょ、ちょっと待ってくれ。
今、火を...」
lines.english: “W-wait. I need to turn off the stove—”

lines.japanese:
「あ～もしもし～。
こちら北原春希の携帯で～」
lines.english: “Hellooo. You’ve reached Haruki Kitahara’s pho-one.”

lines.japanese:
「うわぁっ！？
やめろやめろ～！」
lines.english: “No! Stop, stop!”

lines.japanese: 「な～んてね」
lines.english: “Just kidding.”

lines.japanese:
「っ...くだらないイタズラはやめんか！
ついこの間、致命的な行き違いを誘発したばかりだろ」
lines.english: “Enough with the stupid pranks! You caused a catastrophic misunderstanding by answering it just the other day.”

lines.japanese:
「や～っぱマズかったんじゃん、この間出ちゃったの。
そういうこと、遠慮なく言ってくれないとさぁ」
lines.english: “So answering it last time did cause trouble. You have to tell me these things, Haruki.”
“…Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「...頭下げる前に出なよ」
lines.english: “…Answer the phone before you bow.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、北原...」
lines.english: “Hello, Kitahara speaking…”

lines.japanese:
「お～元気してっか春希？
今、依緒と近くのコンビニまで来てるんだけどさ～、
お前んとこ酒あるか～？」
lines.english: “Hey, Haruki! How’s it going? Io and I are at the convenience store nearby. You got any booze at your place?”

lines.japanese: 「武也？」
lines.english: “Takeya?”

lines.japanese:
「え？　いや、今日はちょっと...
だから冬休みまでにレポート提出しないと」
lines.english: “What? No, tonight’s not a good time… I have to get this paper handed in before winter break.”

lines.japanese: 俺のじゃないけどな。
lines.english: It wasn’t my paper, of course.

lines.japanese:
「だったらまだ一週間もあるじゃん。
たまにはいいだろたまには？」
lines.english: “That’s still a whole week away. We can do this once in a while, can’t we?”

lines.japanese:
「今までそう言ってきたせいで、
とっくに締め切り過ぎてて今度が最終期限なんだよ」
lines.english: “Saying ‘once in a while’ every time is why the deadline passed ages ago and this is the final extension.”

lines.japanese: 俺がじゃないけどな。
lines.english: Not that I’m the one who missed it.

lines.japanese:
「そういう大げさなこと言っといて、
数日間のバッファ隠し持ってるのが春希だよな～。
何年つきあってると思ってんだよ？　俺を侮るなよ？」
lines.english: “You always make things sound desperate while secretly keeping a few days in reserve. How many years have we known each other? Don’t underestimate me.”
“Ha ha…”

lines.japanese: だから、俺じゃないんだってば。
lines.english: I’m telling you, it wasn’t mine.

lines.japanese:
「とにかく、もうつまみとか買い込んじまったんだよ。
あとお前の部屋まで歩いて５分なの」
lines.english: “Anyway, we already bought a mountain of snacks, and we’re five minutes from your apartment.”

lines.japanese:
「そりゃよかった。
そこから駅まで徒歩６分だ」
lines.english: “Excellent. The station is six minutes from where you are.”

lines.japanese:
「どうしても行ったら駄目か？
ほんの一時間でもいいんだけどな」
lines.english: “You really won’t let us come over? Even for an hour?”

lines.japanese:
「一時間だけ飲むつもりならお薦めの場所があるぞ。
駅前の『半魚人』という...」
lines.english: “If you only want an hour, I know the perfect place. It’s a bar by the station called the Merman—”

lines.japanese:
「わかった、わかったよ！
...ったく、友達甲斐ないなぁ。
せっかくお前んちの夕飯たかってやろうと思ったのに」
lines.english: “All right, all right! Some friend you are. And here I was going to do you the favor of eating your dinner.”

lines.japanese: 「それが友達甲斐のある奴の言うことか？」
lines.english: “Is that your idea of being a good friend?”

lines.japanese:
「じゃあ、今日は諦めて帰るけどよ。
...その前に、ちょっとだけ聞いていいか？」
lines.english: “Fine, we’ll give up and go home. But first, can I ask you one thing?”

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese:
「ちゃんと飯食ってるか？　寝てるか？
...自堕落な生活送ってないだろうな？」
lines.english: “Are you eating enough? Are you sleeping? You’re not letting yourself go to hell, are you?”
“Oh…”

lines.japanese: そっか...
lines.english: Of course.

lines.japanese:
このタイミングで武也が押しかけようとしてるのは、
ちゃんとした意味があったんだ。
lines.english: Takeya had a real reason for trying to force his way in tonight.

lines.japanese:
「出来ればでいいんだけどさ、
５分だけ、話だけでもしないか？
...玄関口でもいいよ」
lines.english: “Only if you feel up to it, but couldn’t we talk for five minutes? We don’t even have to come past the door.”
“Takeya…”

lines.japanese: 土曜の夜、武也や依緒を巻き込んだ、俺の騒乱。
lines.english: The chaos I had dragged Takeya and Io into on Saturday night.

lines.japanese:
きっとその後、雪菜から謝罪とともに聞いたはずの、
うわべだけの事の顛末。
lines.english: The superficial version of how it all ended, which Setsuna must have told them afterward along with her apologies.

lines.japanese:
つまりこいつらも、
麻理さんや杉浦と同じ...
lines.english: So they were the same as Mari and Sugiura…

lines.japanese:
「買っちまったつまみ、持って帰るの面倒なんだよ。
受け取ってくれよ」
lines.english: “It’s a pain carrying all these snacks home. At least take them off our hands.”

lines.japanese:
ったくこいつら、
どれだけ俺のこと信用してないんだよ...
lines.english: Honestly, these people… How little faith did they have in me?

lines.japanese: どれだけ、俺のこと...
lines.english: How much did they care about me…?

lines.japanese:
「武也、あのさ...
俺、今からそっちに...え」
lines.english: “Takeya, listen… I’ll come meet you right—what?”
“Oh…”

lines.japanese: と、その時、俺の肩が二度ほど叩かれた。
lines.english: Just then, someone tapped my shoulder twice.

lines.japanese:
つられて向けた視線の先には、
もうとっくにコートを着込み、
帰り支度万端の和泉が立っていた。
lines.english: I turned, and there stood Izumi, already buttoned into her coat and completely ready to leave.

lines.japanese:
「どした春希？
何だって～？」
lines.english: “What was that, Haruki? You’re coming where?”

lines.japanese:
にっこり笑いながら、
『バイバイ』って手を振る和泉が、立っていた。
lines.english: There stood Izumi, smiling as she raised a hand in farewell.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、ね」
lines.english: “See you.”

lines.japanese: 「別に、断ったのに」
lines.english: “But I already told them no.”

lines.japanese: 「今の春希にとっては、断らない方がいいかなって」
lines.english: “I thought maybe it would be better for you if you didn’t.”
“Izumi…”

lines.japanese:
結局和泉は、
できたての激辛カレーに一口も手を付けることなく、
信じられないことに『腹ペコで』帰宅しようとしていた。
lines.english: And so, without touching a single bite of the freshly made extra-hot curry, Izumi prepared—unbelievably—to go home ‘starving.’

lines.japanese:
「また今週のどっかで来るわ。
来週から冬休み入っちゃうから、その前ね」
lines.english: “I’ll come over again sometime this week. Winter break starts next week, so before then.”

lines.japanese: 「そう、か」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、よろしく」
lines.english: “Good. I’m counting on you.”

lines.japanese:
つまり、武也や依緒が、俺のことを心配して、
ここに押しかけようとしたように...
lines.english: Takeya and Io had tried to come here because they were worried about me…

lines.japanese:
和泉が今、この場所を去ろうとするのも、
結局、あいつらとまるで同じ理由なんじゃないかって...
lines.english: And perhaps Izumi was leaving now for exactly the same reason.

lines.japanese: 「なぁ、和泉...」
lines.english: “Izumi…”

lines.japanese: 「あんたの周りって面白いね、春希」
lines.english: “The people around you are fascinating, Haruki.”
“Huh…?”

lines.japanese:
「あんたって誰にでも面倒見がよくってさ、
一生懸命で、頑張ってるんだけど、
いつも与えてばかりで損してるって思ってた」
lines.english: “You’re always looking after everyone. You work so hard, and you’re always giving, so I thought you were the one who always lost out.”

lines.japanese:
「そりゃ、お前はそう思うだろうな。
何しろ搾取する側の筆頭だし」
lines.english: “Naturally you would. You exploit me more than anyone.”

lines.japanese:
「ところが実は全然そうじゃないんだね。
色んな人が、男も女も、春希に与えようとする。
...ホント、面白い」
lines.english: “But I was completely wrong. All kinds of people—men and women—are trying to give something back to you. It really is fascinating.”

lines.japanese:
「お前が一番面白いわ。
俺の周囲では」
lines.english: “You’re the most interesting person I know.”

lines.japanese:
「ホント面白い。ワクワクする。
あんたたちの関係、単純で複雑で、すごく勉強になるよ」
lines.english: “It’s fascinating. I can’t wait to see what happens.All your relationships are so simple and so complicated. I’m learning a lot.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　何だって？」
lines.english: “What? What did you say?”

lines.japanese: 「春希のこと、やっぱ好きだなって」
lines.english: “I said I really do like you, Haruki.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
「今の秘密だからね？　特にあんたには。
...あんたにだけ言うんだからね？」
lines.english: “That’s a secret, all right? Especially from you. I’m telling you and only you.”

lines.japanese:
「お前...
やっぱ俺のこと馬鹿にしてるだろ？」
lines.english: “You’re making fun of me again, aren’t you?”

lines.japanese:
「いいや本当だよ。
面倒見のいい奴って...好きだよ」
lines.english: “No, I mean it. I like people who take care of others.”
“What…”

lines.japanese: 瞬間...
lines.english: In that instant…

lines.japanese: 和泉の表情が、一変した。
lines.english: Izumi’s entire expression changed.

lines.japanese: ように、俺には見えた。
lines.english: Or so it appeared to me.

lines.japanese: 「あたしって、実はかなりの甘えん坊なんだ」
lines.english: “The truth is, I’m terribly needy.”
“I-Izumi…?”

lines.japanese:
「だから、頼れる人に焦がれる。
恋焦がれて、もっとワガママ言いたくなる」
lines.english: “That’s why I long for someone I can depend on. And when that longing turns to love, I want to ask for more and more.”
“H-hey…”

lines.japanese:
「そんなあたしのワガママを、
一生懸命頑張って叶えてくれる人が好き。大好き」
lines.english: “I love a man who’ll do everything he can to grant every selfish thing I ask of him. I love him so much.”

lines.japanese:
和泉の、あたたかな両手が、
俺の頬を両側から挟み込む。
lines.english: Izumi’s warm hands cupped my cheeks.

lines.japanese:
「口うるさいんだけど、ぶつくさ文句は言うんだけど、
それでも絶対に見捨てたりしない」
lines.english: “He nags me, and he complains under his breath, but no matter what, he never abandons me.”

lines.japanese:
その瞳に映る黒は真剣な光をたたえてて、
その奥に映る俺の、かなり滑稽なうろたえた表情までも、
しっかりとあぶり出す。
lines.english: Her dark eyes shone with an intensity that brought even my ridiculous, flustered reflection into sharp focus.

lines.japanese:
「誰にでも平等に優しくて、けれどあたしには、
ほんの少しひいきしてくれたりすると最高かな」
lines.english: “He’s equally kind to everyone. But if he favored me just a tiny bit, that would be perfect.”

lines.japanese: 「やめろ...冗談は」
lines.english: “Stop… Don’t joke about this.”

lines.japanese: 「冗談だって、思う？」
lines.english: “You think I’m joking?”

lines.japanese: なんだか、和泉と話してる気がしない。
lines.english: I no longer felt as if I were talking to Izumi.

lines.japanese:
こいつは、和泉千晶って奴は、
こんな、深くて黒くて静かな激情を抱え込む、
そんな種類の『女』なんかじゃないはずで。
lines.english: Chiaki Izumi wasn’t supposed to be that kind of ‘woman’—not the kind who harbored such deep, dark, quiet passion.

lines.japanese:
逆に、そういう『女』と対極にいるからこそ、
俺の側にいても、苦しさを感じない希有な友人で。
lines.english: It was precisely because she was the opposite of that kind of ‘woman’ that she was the rare friend I could be around without pain.

lines.japanese: なのにこれは...こんなのは。
lines.english: And yet this… This was…

lines.japanese:
俺の知っている和泉じゃなくて、
けれど、俺の知っている...
lines.english: Not the Izumi I knew, and yet someone I knew…

lines.japanese: 「...冗談だけどね」
lines.english: “…Just kidding.”

lines.japanese: 「だよなぁぁぁぁっ！！！」
lines.english: “I knew it!”

lines.japanese:
やっぱり根に持ってたんだな...
カレー食えなかったこと。
lines.english: She really had been holding a grudge about missing the curry.

lines.japanese: 「あ、と...すいません」
lines.english: “Oh—sorry.”

lines.japanese:
「っ！？
い、いえ、こちらこそ」
lines.english: “Ah! N-no, I’m sorry.”
“…Hm? Wait. That girl…”

lines.japanese:
「かなり高めのストライクゾーンだったね。
あんたの」
lines.english: “She was pretty high in your strike zone.”

lines.japanese:
「いや、そうでなく...
いや、絶好球ってのはそうなんだけど。
どこかで見たような...？」
lines.english: “That’s not what I—though yes, she was right down the middle. I feel like I’ve seen her somewhere.”

lines.japanese:
「ウチの大学のコでしょ。
この辺りに住んでる学生なんて」
lines.english: “She probably goes to our university. Most students living around here do.”

lines.japanese: 「それだけ...かなぁ」
lines.english: “Is that all it is…?”

lines.japanese: 「かんぱ～い！」
lines.english: “Cheers!”

lines.japanese:
「うわ辛っ！？
辛いぞこのカレー」
lines.english: “God, that’s hot! This curry is vicious.”

lines.japanese:
「げ、ほんとだ。しかも真っ赤だし。
どれだけスパイス入れたらこんなになるのよ」
lines.english: “It really is. And it’s bright red. How much spice did you put in this?”

lines.japanese:
「なら食うな。
俺にはちょうどいいんだ」
lines.english: “Then don’t eat it. It’s just right for me.”
…It burned.

lines.japanese:
「い、いや...でもこの辛さがビールに合うこと！
進む進む」
lines.english: “N-no, it’s fine. This heat goes beautifully with beer. I can’t stop drinking.”

lines.japanese:
酒とつまみをコンビニ袋にどっさり詰めて現れた二人組は、
まずはいきなり我が家の鍋に突撃した。
lines.english: The pair had arrived with convenience-store bags bulging with drinks and snacks, then launched an immediate assault on the pot in my kitchen.

lines.japanese:
「あたしはご飯あった方がいいな。
ねぇ春希、生卵ない？」
lines.english: “I want mine with rice. Haruki, do you have a raw egg?”

lines.japanese: ...もしかして、本当に晩飯たかりに来ただけなのか？
lines.english: Had they really come over just to mooch dinner?

lines.japanese:
「全部食うなよ？
週末までこれで食いつなぐつもりなんだから」
lines.english: “Don’t finish it. I planned to live on this until the weekend.”

lines.japanese: そういえば最近、週の半分がカレーだ...
lines.english: Come to think of it, I’d been eating curry half the week lately.

lines.japanese:
これもレパートリーのなさによるものか、
自分をも巻き込んだ嫌がらせの賜物か。
lines.english: Was this the price of my limited repertoire, or had my petty revenge against her managed to catch me in the crossfire?

lines.japanese: 「にしても、ここにお邪魔するのも久しぶりだね」
lines.english: “It’s been a long time since we came over.”

lines.japanese:
「春希が一人暮らし始めたって聞いたときには、
毎日のように通い詰める予定だったんだけどな」
lines.english: “When I heard Haruki was living alone, I planned to make this my second home.”

lines.japanese:
「もしそんなことしやがったら、
来るたびに掃除させるからな」
lines.english: “Try it and I’ll make you clean the place every time you come.”

lines.japanese:
「転部しちゃってからは特にご無沙汰だもんね。
やっぱ毎日顔合わせてないと調子出ないよ」
lines.english: “We’ve hardly seen you since you changed departments. Things just aren’t the same when we don’t see each other every day.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ...ごめん」
lines.english: “Uh… yeah. Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「おい、依緒」
lines.english: “Oi, Io.”
“Oh…”

lines.japanese:
空気を読んだ...というか読み過ぎた武也が、
即座に依緒を肘でつつく。
lines.english: Takeya read the room—or overread it—and immediately nudged Io with his elbow.

lines.japanese:
そういえば三年に進級するとき、
誰にも相談せずに転部を決めたこと、
依緒に随分責められたっけな。
lines.english: Come to think of it, Io had been furious when I changed departments before our third year without consulting anyone.

lines.japanese:
「気にするな。
あの時のことは俺も悪かったって思ってる」
lines.english: “Don’t worry about it. I know I was in the wrong back then too.”

lines.japanese: 「...とお前に思わせたことがそもそも失敗なわけ」
lines.english: “…Getting you to think that at all is where we went wrong.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
「今日の俺たちは、ただ飲みに来ただけなんだから、
湿っぽい方向に話持ってったらペナルティって、
来る前にルール決めてたんだよ」
lines.english: “We came here tonight strictly to drink. Before we left, we agreed that anyone who steered the conversation somewhere gloomy would pay a penalty.”

lines.japanese:
「このまま武也がミスらなかったら、
今日の酒代全部あたし持ち...」
lines.english: “If Takeya made it through the whole night without slipping, I was going to pay for all the alcohol…”

lines.japanese: 「...その勝負の方がよっぽど俺に失礼じゃないか？」
lines.english: “…Isn’t that bet far more insulting to me?”

lines.japanese:
...やっぱ、
本当に晩飯たかりに来ただけなんだろうか？
lines.english: Maybe they really had come over just to mooch dinner.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そういえばさ、依緒」
lines.english: “Oh, that reminds me, Io.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　なに？」
lines.english: “Hm? What?”

lines.japanese:
「『おい、依緒』って回文だな。
今まで気づかなかったけど」
lines.english: “‘Oi, Io’ is a palindrome. I never noticed.”
“…Takeya.”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese:
「おい何やってんだよ武也？
ひとんちの引き出しを勝手に開けるな」
lines.english: “What are you doing, Takeya? Stop opening other people’s drawers.”

lines.japanese:
「何言ってんだよ。
ひとんち来たらまずは探索ってのは基本だろ」
lines.english: “What are you talking about? The first rule of visiting someone’s house is to search the place.”

lines.japanese: 「中学生かお前は」
lines.english: “Are you twelve?”

lines.japanese:
「な、春希、無修正ＡＶとかあるか？
上映会やろうぜ上映会」
lines.english: “Hey, Haruki, got any uncensored porn? Let’s have a screening.”

lines.japanese:
「二度も言わせるな。
中学生かお前は」
lines.english: “Don’t make me say it again. Are you twelve?”

lines.japanese: 「お前は同行者の性別を何だと思ってるんだ？」
lines.english: “Have you forgotten you brought a woman with you?”

lines.japanese: 「別にいいじゃん。依緒なんだし」
lines.english: “Who cares? It’s only Io.”

lines.japanese: 「別にいいのか？」
lines.english: “You really don’t mind?”

lines.japanese:
「別にいいさ。
どうせ春希がそんなもの持ってるとも思えないし」
lines.english: “Not really. It’s not like you own anything like that anyway.”

lines.japanese: 「...信頼あるんだな俺」
lines.english: “…It’s good to know you trust me.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、ある意味ね」
lines.english: “In a manner of speaking.”

lines.japanese: 「くっそ～、ないなぁ」
lines.english: “Damn. Nothing.”

lines.japanese:
そんな冷めた会話とは裏腹に、
武也はまだ俺の本棚やベッドの下を漁っている。
lines.english: In stark contrast to our indifferent exchange, Takeya was still rummaging through my shelves and under my bed.

lines.japanese:
いい具合に酒が回ってるとは言え、
今の武也を『曜日ごとの彼女たち』が見たら、
三か月くらいの恋も一瞬で醒めるに違いない。
lines.english: He was pleasantly drunk, but if any of his weekday girlfriends could see him now, even a three-month romance would die on the spot.

lines.japanese:
ま、武也の場合、ここにいるのが依緒だからこそ、
わざと身も蓋もない態度を取ってるんだろうな。
lines.english: Then again, Takeya was probably being deliberately crude precisely because the woman here was Io.

lines.japanese:
依緒に対してだけは、本当に態度が中学生まんまだし、
その空回りっぷりも痛々しいことこの上ないな...
lines.english: With Io—the one he actually wanted—he reverted completely to a twelve-year-old. Watching all that effort go nowhere was almost painful.
lines.japaneseRuby:
[R依緒^ほんめい]に対してだけは、本当に態度が中学生まんまだし、
その空回りっぷりも痛々しいことこの上ないな...

lines.japanese:
「そっか...最近だったら
ネットから動画をダウンロードってパターンだな。
まずはブックマークをチェック！」
lines.english: “Wait. These days people download their videos. Time to inspect the bookmarks!”

lines.japanese:
「やめろぉぉ～！
馬鹿野郎～！」
lines.english: “Stop! You idiot!”
“…Haruki?”

lines.japanese:
「やっだな～も～。
本当だって、男。付属時代のツレの家なんだって」
lines.english: “Oh, come on. I swear it’s a guy. I’m at an old friend’s place from Houjou High.”

lines.japanese:
「マジでゴメン。今日だけは行けない。
来週は絶対に...え？　明日？」
lines.english: “I’m really sorry. I just can’t make it tonight. Next week, definitely… What? Tomorrow?”

lines.japanese:
「いや、明日はちょっと...
いや、しばらくこいつの側にいないとさぁ。
なんか女にフられて死にたいとか言ってんだよね」
lines.english: “No, tomorrow’s difficult too. I need to stay with this guy for a while. Some woman dumped him and now he says he wants to die.”

lines.japanese: 「...遠慮なく彼女の方に行っていいんだぞ」
lines.english: “…Feel free to go to your girlfriend.”

lines.japanese:
「え？　女？
やっだな～、そんなのいるわけないじゃん。
静子ちゃんだけだって...何回言わせるのこれ？」
lines.english: “What? Another woman? Don’t be silly. There’s nobody but you, Shizuko. How many times do I have to say it?”

lines.japanese: 「...ま、武也にとっての女はいないな、確かに」
lines.english: “…True. Takeya doesn’t have a woman, singular.”

lines.japanese:
「だからさぁ...泣くなって、ほら。
いい？　今から俺が言うことよく聞いて？
.........愛してる、君だけだ」
lines.english: “Come on, don’t cry. Listen carefully to what I’m about to say, all right? …I love you. You’re the only one.”

lines.japanese: 「...おい、いいのかあれ？」
lines.english: “…Should he be saying that?”

lines.japanese: 「なんであたしがいい悪いの判断をする必要がある？」
lines.english: “Why should I be the one to decide what he may or may not say?”

lines.japanese:
「少しは妬いてやったら？
あいつ、結構わざとだぞ？」
lines.english: “You could at least act jealous. He’s laying it on pretty thick on purpose, you know.”

lines.japanese:
「あたしは自分だけを見てくれる男がいいの。
武也と春希だったら、まだ後者を選ぶね」
lines.english: “I want a man with eyes for me alone. Given a choice between Takeya and you, I’d still choose you.”
“…Honestly.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、澄代ちゃん？
俺俺、武也～」
lines.english: “Oh, Sumiyo? It’s me, Takeya.”

lines.japanese: 「...ほれ、ロック」
lines.english: “…Here. On the rocks.”
“Mm.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、どうぞ」
lines.english: “Here you are.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、せんべいじゃなくてイカ」
lines.english: “Oh, and squid, not rice crackers.”

lines.japanese: 「ほい」
lines.english: “Here.”

lines.japanese: 「サンキュ」
lines.english: “Thanks.”
“Phew…”
“…Hey.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「どしたの春希？」
lines.english: “What is it, Haruki?”

lines.japanese: 「そろそろ日付が変わるぞ？」
lines.english: “It’s almost midnight, you know.”

lines.japanese: 「もう変わってるな。３分経った」
lines.english: “It already is. By three minutes.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、テレビつけていい？
確か衛星でＮＢＡのゲームが...」
lines.english: “Mind if I turn on the television? I think there’s an NBA game on satellite…”

lines.japanese: 「確か駅で電車の終電が...」
lines.english: “I think there was something at the station called the last train…”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫、雑魚寝で」
lines.english: “We’re fine sleeping on the floor.”

lines.japanese:
「その代わりエアコンだけは強くしといて。
ついでに加湿器があると最高」
lines.english: “Just keep the heat up. A humidifier would be perfect too.”

lines.japanese:
「そうじゃないかとは思ってたけど、
お前ら帰らないつもりかよ...」
lines.english: “I suspected as much, but you two really don’t mean to leave, do you?”

lines.japanese:
「いいじゃんか。
こんなに気を使わずに酔える飲みなんか、
ここしばらく全然なかったんだぞ？」
lines.english: “Come on. I haven’t had a carefree night of drinking like this in ages.”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃお前が虎視眈々としすぎてるからで...」
lines.english: “That’s because you’re always on the prowl—”

lines.japanese:
「普通に飲んで騒ぐだけなら
気を使う必要なんかないんだけどねぇ」
lines.english: “If you only wanted to drink and make noise, there’d be no reason to watch yourself.”

lines.japanese:
「そんなの俺狙いのコたちに失礼じゃん。
ほんとお前ら何もわかってないんだから...」
lines.english: “That would be rude to all the girls who are after me. You two understand nothing.”

lines.japanese: 「わかりたくもないわ」
lines.english: “And I don’t want to.”

lines.japanese: 「ん...むぅ...すぅぅぅぅ...」
lines.english: “Mm… nnngh… zzz…”

lines.japanese:
「ほら毛布。
せめてこれ羽織ってろ」
lines.english: “Here’s a blanket. At least cover yourself with this.”

lines.japanese: 「ん～...くぅぅぅぅ...」
lines.english: “Mmm… zzz…”

lines.japanese: 「だらしない」
lines.english: “Pathetic.”

lines.japanese: 一人沈没。
lines.english: One down.

lines.japanese:
「依緒はまだ平気か？
ベッド使っていいんだぞ？」
lines.english: “Are you still all right, Io? You can use the bed.”

lines.japanese:
「いいよ。
彼女でもない女の匂い付けてんなって」
lines.english: “No. You don’t want some woman who isn’t your girlfriend leaving her scent on it.”

lines.japanese: 「別にそんなこと気にしないけどな」
lines.english: “I wouldn’t care.”

lines.japanese: つい先週とっくに付けられてるんで。
lines.english: That ship had sailed the week before.
“Phew…”

lines.japanese:
「まだ飲むか？
作るけど」
lines.english: “Want another drink? I can make one.”

lines.japanese: 「いい...ちょっと休む」
lines.english: “No… I’m taking a break.”

lines.japanese: 「そか」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 俺たち三人の強さは、昔から結構トントンだった。
lines.english: The three of us had always been fairly evenly matched when it came to drinking.

lines.japanese:
ただ、ここにあと一人加わると、
そのバランスは一気に崩壊してたっけ。
lines.english: Add one more person, however, and that balance used to collapse completely.
“Mm… mmm…”
“…Right.”

lines.japanese:
日をまたいだ辺りから、まったりし始めた空気は、
一人が欠けることにより、さらに沈滞を始めた。
lines.english: The atmosphere had begun to mellow around midnight. With one of us down, it sank even deeper into stillness.

lines.japanese:
俺も依緒も、ちょっと重めのまぶたを持て余し、
ただ、酒を飲んだり壁や天井をぼうっと眺めたりしてた。
lines.english: Io and I struggled with our heavy eyelids, drinking now and then or staring vaguely at the walls and ceiling.

lines.japanese:
でも本当は、そうやってぼうっとしてることに、
お互い満足してるわけじゃない。
lines.english: But neither of us was truly content simply to sit there in a haze.

lines.japanese:
俺は依緒が口火を切るのを、
依緒は自分が口火を切るのを、
きっと、今か今かと待っていた。
lines.english: I was waiting for Io to begin. Io seemed to be waiting for herself to begin too.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ」
lines.english: “Listen…”

lines.japanese: 「そうか」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「...まだ何も言ってないんだけど？」
lines.english: “…I haven’t said anything yet.”
“…Sorry.”

lines.japanese:
だからあまりにも『来た！』と意気込みすぎたらしい。
ちょっと恥ずかしかった。
lines.english: Apparently I’d been so keyed up for the moment that I’d jumped the gun. It was a little embarrassing.

lines.japanese:
「実はさ...
あたしたち、昨日は雪菜の家に行って来たんだ」
lines.english: “The truth is… we went to Setsuna’s house yesterday.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: そう、ここが正しい。
lines.english: There. That was the right place for it.

lines.japanese:
「あそこは親がいるから、
１１時頃にはちゃんと帰ったけどな」
lines.english: “Her parents were there, so we made sure to leave around eleven.”

lines.japanese: 「元気に...してたか？」
lines.english: “Was she… doing all right?”

lines.japanese: ほんの数日前に会ったばかりなのに。
lines.english: Though I had seen her only days before.

lines.japanese:
その時の雪菜の表情が、声が、言葉が、
俺の頭に染みついて離れてくれないくせに。
lines.english: Though her face, her voice, and her words that night were etched into my mind and refused to leave.

lines.japanese:
それでもやっぱり、１日前の雪菜の様子が、
ずっとずっと、気になってた。
lines.english: Even so, I couldn’t stop wondering what Setsuna had been like only yesterday.

lines.japanese:
「最初に顔見たときにはさ...
今の春希より、ずっと落ち込んでた」
lines.english: “When we first saw her… she was much more depressed than you are now.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、お前たちが帰る頃には？」
lines.english: “And by the time you left?”

lines.japanese: 「...今の春希より、少し落ち込んでた、かな？」
lines.english: “…Still a little more depressed than you are now, I suppose.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 『やっぱり怒ってくれないんだ...』
lines.english: “So you still won’t get angry with me…”

lines.japanese:
『叱っても、説教もしてくれないんだ...
昔みたいに、してくれないんだぁ...っ』
lines.english: “You won’t scold me. You won’t lecture me… Not the way you used to…”

lines.japanese:
今まで何度繰り返したかわからない、
誤解と思い込みと、悲しいすれ違いの果ての
雪菜の涙は、確かに俺の胸をえぐってた。
lines.english: Setsuna’s tears, born of more misunderstandings, mistaken assumptions, and painful failures to reach each other than I could count, had cut deep into my heart.

lines.japanese:
けれど、俺のそんな程度の痛みなんて、
所詮、ほんの二次災害に過ぎないんだ。
lines.english: But whatever pain I felt was collateral damage at most.

lines.japanese: 「春希さぁ」
lines.english: “Haruki.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「あんたって、結構強いんだね」
lines.english: “You’re stronger than I thought.”

lines.japanese:
その言葉そのものには、
一見、肯定的な意味が込められてるように思えるけど。
lines.english: Taken by itself, the remark might have sounded like praise.

lines.japanese:
残念ながら、その言い方には、
そんなニュアンスが込められてるようには聞こえなかった。
lines.english: Unfortunately, nothing in the way she said it sounded remotely approving.

lines.japanese: 「雪菜はさ...また『自分のせいだ』って」
lines.english: “Setsuna was saying again that everything was her fault.”
“I see…”

lines.japanese:
ただ、誘われてパーティに参加したことを。
誰にも連絡せず、門限を破ってしまったことを。
lines.english: Going to the party because she had been invited. Breaking curfew without contacting anyone.

lines.japanese:
「なんでもかんでも『自分のせい』。
三日前も、一年前も、三年前だって...」
lines.english: “Everything is always ‘her fault.’ Three days ago, a year ago, even three years ago…”

lines.japanese:
俺たちが、三人でいられなくなってしまったことも。
...三人になったことすらも。
lines.english: That the three of us could no longer be together. That there had ever been three of us at all.

lines.japanese:
「だから慰めても責めても落ち込むんだ。
...難儀な女になっちゃったなぁ」
lines.english: “So whether we comfort her or blame her, she only sinks deeper. She’s become a real handful.”

lines.japanese:
だけど、雪菜がそう思い込むようになったのは、
元を正せば俺のせい。
lines.english: But I was the reason Setsuna had learned to think that way in the first place.

lines.japanese: 「でもさ、お前も難儀だよ、春希」
lines.english: “You’re a real handful too, Haruki.”

lines.japanese: 「そう、かな？」
lines.english: “Am I?”

lines.japanese:
「他のことならいくらでも平気で人を非難するくせに、
ことこの件に関してだけは、
絶対に雪菜の非を認めようとしないじゃないか」
lines.english: “You condemn people without a second thought over anything else. But when it comes to this one thing, you absolutely refuse to admit that Setsuna did anything wrong.”

lines.japanese:
だって、そんな虚しい『鶏が先か卵が先か』の論争は、
もう、とっくの昔に破綻してる。
lines.english: Because the futile argument over which came first, the chicken or the egg, had collapsed long ago.

lines.japanese:
「俺はいつも公正なだけだ。
...俺が悪いのは自明の理なんだから」
lines.english: “I’m only being fair. It’s self-evident that I’m the one at fault.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、まぁ...実際お前が悪いんだけどな」
lines.english: “W-well… you actually are at fault.”

lines.japanese:
けど、どちらの罪がより重いかという論争は、
あまりにも結果がハッキリしすぎてるから、
雪菜は、絶対に触れようとしない。
lines.english: But Setsuna would never touch the question of whose guilt was greater, because the answer was far too obvious.

lines.japanese: 「ありがとうな、依緒」
lines.english: “Thank you, Io.”

lines.japanese: 「かばってないぞ？」
lines.english: “I’m not defending you.”

lines.japanese: 「俺のところ、来てくれて」
lines.english: “For coming here.”

lines.japanese:
「...いや、それよりも、
雪菜のとこ、行ってくれて」
lines.english: “…No—more importantly, for going to see Setsuna.”
“…Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
俺は、十分恵まれてた。
だって、これで四組目だ。
lines.english: I was surrounded by plenty of people who cared. That made four groups in all.

lines.japanese:
ここ数日で、色んな人たちの介入を受けて、
深く思い悩む暇もなかった。
lines.english: So many people had intervened over the past few days that I’d barely had time to brood.

lines.japanese:
俺には、励ましてくれる、介入してくれる、
からかってくれる、そして責めてくれる人たちがいた。
lines.english: I had people who encouraged me, interfered with me, teased me, and held me to account.

lines.japanese:
「なぁ、依緒。
これからも、雪菜のことよろしく頼むな」
lines.english: “Io… keep looking after Setsuna for me.”

lines.japanese:
けれど雪菜には、依緒と武也しかいなかった。
...だから、今の俺より、ずっと落ち込んでたんだ。
lines.english: Setsuna, by contrast, had only Io and Takeya. That was why she had been so much more depressed than I was.

lines.japanese:
端から見ると、あんなに社交的で華やかな奴なのに、
今の雪菜は、俺以上に人との関わり合いを拒絶してる。
lines.english: To anyone looking in, she seemed so sociable and radiant. Yet now Setsuna was shutting other people out even more thoroughly than I was.

lines.japanese:
ただ俺より誤魔化し方が上手いから、
俺たち以外には気づかれていないだけ。
lines.english: She was simply better at hiding it, so no one but us had noticed.

lines.japanese:
「今は任せとけ。
...その代わり、早く引き取れよ。
あたしたちは、あくまでも代理なんだからな？」
lines.english: “Leave her to us for now. But take over again soon. We’re only standing in for you, remember?”

lines.japanese:
「...お前らも相当にお節介だな。
俺のこと全然言えないな」
lines.english: “…You two are terrible busybodies yourselves. You have no right to criticize me.”

lines.japanese:
「春希が自分で呼び寄せたんだ。
自分の同類を」
lines.english: “You summoned us yourself, Haruki. Kindred spirits.”
“Io…”

lines.japanese: 「すぅぅ...ふぅぅ...」
lines.english: “Zzz… hff…”
“Mm… mmm… zzz…”

lines.japanese: 二人沈没。
lines.english: Two down.

lines.japanese:
今はもう、夜中の３時。
...つまり水曜２７時。
lines.english: It was already three in the morning—which still belonged, in my mind, to Wednesday night.

lines.japanese:
ほんの数日間、特別になって、
ほんの数日前、特別の座から転がり落ちた、
俺たちの、他とは違う時刻。
lines.english: Our own peculiar hour—one that had been special for only a handful of days, and had lost that status only days ago.

lines.japanese:
だからまた、ここから始める。
...そのくらいの取っ掛かりがないと、
とてもこんな勇気は振り絞れないから。
lines.english: So I would begin again here. Without a foothold like this, I could never have summoned the courage.

lines.japanese:
酒の力でもなんでも借りてみせる。
雪菜と、もう一度言葉を繋ぐために。
lines.english: If that was what it took to start talking to Setsuna again, I’d take whatever courage the alcohol could give me.

lines.japanese: 『今、武也と依緒が来てる』
lines.english: “Takeya and Io are here.”

lines.japanese:
三年前に戻りたいって、そう思ってた。
今から逃げ出したいって、そう願ってた。
lines.english: I had wanted to turn back the clock three years. I had wished I could escape the present.

lines.japanese: けれど...
lines.english: But…

lines.japanese:
俺はやっぱりこの時間に...
あれから三年後の世界に、生きてなくちゃならない。
lines.english: I had to live here—in the world three years on from then.

lines.japanese: 今の雪菜がいる、この時間に存在しなくちゃならない。
lines.english: Here, in the present, with Setsuna as she was now.

lines.japanese:
『人んちの晩飯食い散らかして、大騒ぎしたあげく、
ガーガー寝てやがる』
lines.english: “They devoured someone else’s dinner, raised hell, and now they’re snoring their heads off.”

lines.japanese:
麻理さん、杉浦、和泉...は置いといて、
依緒に武也、そして、そこから繋がる外の世界。
lines.english: Mari, Sugiura, Izumi—well, leave Izumi aside—then Io and Takeya, and the wider world they connected me to.

lines.japanese:
ここには、三年前に負けず劣らず、
お節介なお人好しが俺の周囲にたくさんいるんだから。
lines.english: Here, too, I had plenty of meddlesome, softhearted people around me—just as many as I had three years ago.

lines.japanese:
『久しぶりに浴びるほど飲んだ。
明日、起きられるかな？』
lines.english: “I haven’t drunk that much in ages. Think I’ll be able to get up tomorrow?”

lines.japanese:
なぁ、雪菜...
今のお前には、たくさんいるか？
そんな大切な人たちが。
lines.english: Setsuna… do you have many people like that around you now—people who matter that much to you?

lines.japanese:
俺が、そうならなくちゃ、いけないか？
俺が、そうなってもいいのか？
...お前を裏切った、この俺が。
lines.english: Do I have to become one of them? Am I allowed to? Me—the man who betrayed you?

lines.japanese:
『今日はそれだけ。もう寝る。
また明日、メールする』
lines.english: “That’s all for tonight. I’m going to sleep. I’ll write again tomorrow.”

lines.japanese:
最後に、一番伝えたかったメッセージを、
さり気なく追加して...
lines.english: I casually tacked on the message I had most wanted to send.

lines.japanese: 「ふあぁ～...っ」
lines.english: “Huaaah…”

lines.japanese:
送信ボタンを押した途端、
一気に強烈な眠気が襲ってくる。
lines.english: The moment I hit Send, sleepiness hit me like a wall.

lines.japanese:
いや、実はとっくに浸食されてたんだけど、
今まで脳が別の思いに囚われすぎてて、
気づかなかっただけ。
lines.english: No, it had been creeping through me for some time. My mind had simply been too occupied by other things to notice.

lines.japanese:
『なんて当たり障りのない』とか、
『もっと伝えるべき事があるだろ』とか、
『お前こそ中学生か』とか。
lines.english:
“Talk about playing it safe.”
“You’ve got more to say than that.”
“Who’s twelve now?”

lines.japanese:
このメールを、
今、目の前で転がってる奴らに見られたら、
そんなふうに呆れられるんだろうな。
lines.english: I knew exactly what the people sprawled out in front of me would say if they saw the message.

lines.japanese:
でも、今日はこれでいい。
だって、もう、こんなに眠い...
lines.english: But for tonight, this was enough. I was already so tired…

lines.japanese:
また話したいことが見つかったら、
明日、メールすればいいんだから。
lines.english: Whenever I found something else I wanted to say, I could write again tomorrow.

lines.japanese:
『依緒と武也くん、
昨日はうちに遊びに来てたよ』
lines.english: “Io and Takeya came to our house yesterday.”

lines.japanese:
『うちだと流石にお父さんの目もあるから、
お酒は駄目だったけど、たくさん話した。
とっても楽しかったな』
lines.english: “Dad was there, so of course we couldn’t drink, but we talked for hours. I had a wonderful time.”

lines.japanese:
『朝、起きれるといいね。
あと、風邪ひかないようにね』
lines.english: “I hope you can get up in the morning. And don’t catch a cold.”

lines.japanese:
『おやすみなさい。
また明日』
lines.english: “Good night. See you tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: 『絶対に、また明日』
lines.english: “Definitely. See you tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: 「ん～...んぐぁぁぁぁぁ...」
lines.english: “Mmm… nnnghh…”

lines.japanese: 「う～...頭痛ぁ」
lines.english: “Ugh… my head.”

lines.japanese:
「やっちゃったぁ...
朝から講義あんのになぁ」
lines.english: “I really did it this time… I have a morning lecture.”

lines.japanese:
「春希の奴...
一人だけ早起きしてさっさと出やがってぇ」
lines.english: “That bastard Haruki… He got up early and left without us.”

lines.japanese:
「ふあぁぁぁ～...ええと、トラベルセット。
買ってきたよね、確か...」
lines.english: “Huaaah… Let’s see, my travel kit. I did buy one, didn’t I?”

lines.japanese: 「あ～、あったあっ...」
lines.english: “Ah, found i—”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「使ってある...」
lines.english: “It’s already been used…”
